chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Sa'd ibn Sa'd from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim ibn al-Fudayl from Hamzah ibn Humran from Dawud ibn Farqad from Humran, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon them both): 'The oath upon which I am bound to pay expiation?' They said: 'Whatever you swore upon, from that which entails obedience to Allah, and you did not do it, then upon you is the expiation for it. And whatever you swore upon, from that which entails disobedience to Allah, then its expiation is leaving it. And whatever was neither disobedience nor obedience, then it is nothing.'
ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for breaking an oath to perform a good deed versus a bad deed?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between oaths of obligation, sin, and neutrality, establishing that the nature of the sworn act dictates the expiation method. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on intent and the specific category of the action, distinguishing it from general oath rules. The ruling underscores that failing an oath of obedience requires material expiation, while breaking an oath of sin is rectified by abstention, highlighting the practical application of Quranic principles in daily conduct.
